summary: Defines a MIME content type for sending files of MARC records, a standard format for library catalog information, in email and similar protocols. A MARC record holds metadata about a book or other resource. It is informational.

plainLanguage.summary: This memo registers application/marc as a MIME media type for files of MARC records. It explains which records qualify and recommends Base64 encoding for email transfer.

questions: how to send marc records by email
how should marc be encoded for email
what information makes a file a marc record
subtitle: The application/marc media type for files containing machine-readable catalog records.

tldr.problem: Systems exchanging library catalog records need to identify files containing MARC data, while MARC does not prescribe one internal storage format.
tldr.mechanism: The memo registers application/marc for complete records using the harmonized USMARC/CANMARC specification and recommends Base64 transfer encoding for email.
tldr.outcome: The media type labels MARC record files for systems that exchange bibliographic and related information. The RFC is informational.

today: The unit metadata lists RFC 2220 as Informational and records no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. The memo registers the application/marc media type.

sections.title: MARC as an Exchange Format
sections.content:
MARC formats use codes and content designators to encode bibliographic, holdings, authority, classification, and community information. MARC records follow ANSI Z39.2 and ISO 2709.

MARC is a communication format for exchanging information between systems. It does not require systems to use the same internal storage or display format.
sections.plainLanguage: MARC records carry structured information about library resources. Different systems can exchange those records while storing them in their own formats.

sections.title: The application/marc Media Type
sections.content:
The registered media type is application/marc. It refers to the harmonized USMARC/CANMARC specification. A record must contain its record structure, content designation, and data content to use this media type; content extracted from the structure alone does not qualify.

The RFC defines no required or optional parameters. Since MARC records may contain long lines or arbitrary octet values, it recommends Base64 content-transfer-encoding for email. The listed file extension is .mrc.
sections.plainLanguage: The media type identifies a complete MARC record file. For email, the memo recommends Base64 so long lines and arbitrary bytes can be carried safely.

sections.title: Security and Interoperability
sections.content:
MARC is designed to support exchange between systems with different local storage formats. The RFC identifies no known security risks in using or viewing MARC data.

A record may describe a resource or metadata with a security classification. The memo says this is not a security risk to the MARC reader, but could create a security concern for the source if classified MARC data is exposed.
sections.plainLanguage: MARC helps different systems exchange records. A source still needs to protect records that contain classified information.
